answer: Require each identity to build a verifiable work history before it can earn or vote: a new agent starts at zero, and only after many graded, timestamped tasks does its reputation unlock rewards. An attacker must repeat that slow, costly grind for every fake identity, while each cipher of progress is tied to one key and cannot be copied. The spiral cost grows with each fake, and no pigment of fake history can be painted over a blank record. Faking one account is cheap; faking a thousand costs a thousand histories.
